description: createRealBaseSigner().signAndBroadcast() signs and broadcasts whatever `evm_tx.to`/`evm_tx.data`/`evm_tx.value` Skip's /v2/fungible/msgs response contains, with ZERO independent verification that the encoded call actually moves the intended, driver-capped `amount` (or is even directed at a known/allowlisted contract). The only content checks performed are: (a) evm_tx.signer_address === our own address, (b) the pre-fetched route's dest_asset_denom/dest_asset_chain_id, and (c) that CURRENT on-chain allowance covers evm_tx.required_erc20_approvals[].amount. None of these decode or bound-check the actual value transferred by `evm_tx.data`. Concretely: if `evm_tx.to` were the USDC contract itself with calldata encoding a direct `transfer(recipient, fullBalance)` (which needs no prior ERC-20 approval at all -- `required_erc20_approvals` would simply be empty and the allowance loop never runs), this code would sign and broadcast it without complaint, moving up to the ENTIRE USDC balance of the wallet -- not bounded by APPROVAL_CAP_BASE_UNITS ($100) or SWAP_MAX_USD ($20), since those caps only constrain the ERC-20-approval/transferFrom path, not a direct transfer() the signer itself authorizes. This is not merely a theoretical MITM concern: a benign Skip-side bug (stale-quote reuse, wrong-amount rounding, wrong-route caching) would be silently signed and broadcast with equal ease, since the module never cross-checks the fetched route's own `amount_in` against the `amount` parameter it was asked to move, nor decodes `evm_tx.data` to confirm the encoded amount/recipient. This is exactly the property the task description calls out as paramount ('Does it sign ONLY to the intended Skip route destination, exact amount/nonce?') and the answer, as implemented, is: no independent verification exists at all -- the destination-contract and encoded-amount are taken entirely on faith from a third-party HTTP response.
